summary: Givens-aware in-schema: extract facts, forbid re-asking
hypothesis: Extracting provided facts first (an easy reading task) and forbidding the 7 questions from re-asking any given should free wasted slots and let the model cover more real unknowns. The bet is that the model's main coverage waste is literally re-stating task-given facts, and that a 3B can reliably do the extraction step even if it can't judge criticality.
technique: A single on-device generate call using a structured in-schema prompt (based on exp011) that includes a `providedFacts` field first — an easy reading-comprehension extraction of facts already stated in the task — followed by the 7 questions, with an absolute rule that none may re-ask any extracted given. No separate refill pass; the whole draw is one coherent generation.
result: Scored 0.287 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), below exp011's best of 0.323, exp003's 0.320, and the baseline 0.307. Coverage stayed at 3 with the same recurring gaps verbatim — the hypothesis was falsified: the 3B's waste is not on slot-for-slot givens restatement but on niche/generic unknowns, so the easy extraction freed little room, and whatever room it freed was refilled with the same generic content, confirming the binding constraint is criticality judgment, not givens-awareness. Discarded.
label: exp025
